oneLiner: 经典力学与微积分奠基人，《原理》建立三定律与万有引力。
oneLinerEn: Founder of classical mechanics and calculus; Principia set the three laws and gravitation.
detail: 1643 年生于英格兰林肯郡的伍尔索普——按当时英国通行的儒略历，生日恰是圣诞节；1661 年入剑桥三一学院，1665 年因大城市鼠疫停课、回乡避居近两年。正是在这段后世称为“奇迹年”的日子里，他同时酝酿出微积分（他自名“流数术”）、光的色散与万有引力三条线索。1672 年他用棱镜把一束白光摊成七色光谱、证明颜色是光与生俱来的属性而非棱镜染上，就此当选皇家学会会员；1668 年他磨镜做出第一台实用的反射式望远镜。1684 年哈雷登门问“行星为何走椭圆”，催成 1687 年由哈雷垫资印行的《自然哲学的数学原理》：他正是从「天体运动与开普勒定律」这一端接起，用一个平方反比的力把苹果落地与月球绕地拧成同一条规律——月球每秒朝地球“下落”约 1.4 毫米，恰合把地面重力按距离平方稀释后的数值，天上与地下第一次被写进同一条「万有引力定律」。他的绝对时空与超距引力被后人奉为铁律两百年，又被爱因斯坦逐条改写；与莱布尼茨的微积分发明权之争撕裂了英国与欧洲大陆数学界近一个世纪。他晚年主持皇家造币厂、督过大规模重铸、也把造假币者送上刑场；1703 年当选皇家学会会长、连任至去世，1704 年出版《光学》，1705 年受封爵士。他留下的炼金术与神学手稿逾百万字，凯恩斯因此说他是“最后一位魔术师”而非“第一个理性主义者”。1727 年辞世，葬于威斯敏斯特教堂，由五位公爵抬棺——这是给一位科学家的、此前只有王侯才享有的哀荣。
detailEn: Born in 1643 at Woolsthorpe in Lincolnshire — by the Julian calendar then used in England, on Christmas Day itself — he entered Trinity College Cambridge in 1661 and in 1665 the university closed for the plague, sending him home for nearly two years. In that “miracle year” he was simultaneously sketching calculus (his “method of fluxions”), the dispersion of light and universal gravitation. In 1672 he spread a beam of white light into a spectrum with a prism and showed that colour is an innate property of light rather than something the prism dyes onto it, winning a Royal Society fellowship; in 1668 he ground the mirrors of the first practical reflecting telescope. Halley’s 1684 question — why do planets move in ellipses? — produced the Principia of 1687, printed with Halley’s own money. Taking the Keplerian orbits as his starting point, one inverse-square force tied the falling apple to the orbiting Moon under a single law of gravitation: the Moon “falls” toward Earth by about 1.4 millimetres each second, exactly the surface gravity thinned by the square of its distance. His absolute space and time and his action at a distance stood as law for two centuries, then were dismantled piece by piece by Einstein; his priority quarrel with Leibniz over calculus split British and continental mathematics for nearly a hundred years. He ran the Royal Mint in his later years, oversaw the great recoinage and hanged forgers; he was elected president of the Royal Society in 1703 and served until he died, published the Opticks in 1704 and was knighted in 1705. He left over a million words of alchemical and theological manuscript, which is why Keynes called him the last of the magicians rather than the first rationalist. He died in 1727 and lay in Westminster Abbey, carried to the grave by five dukes — a mourning until then reserved for princes.

oneLiner: 狭义与广义相对论、光电效应，重塑时空与引力观。
oneLinerEn: Special & general relativity and the photoelectric effect reshaped space, time and gravity.
detail: 1905 年，他坐在伯尔尼专利局三级技术员的工位上，一年之内写出四篇改变物理的论文外加一篇博士论文：光电效应、布朗运动、狭义相对论，以及随后补上一页纸的质能等价「质能方程」。这些全靠两条公设撑起——物理定律在所有「惯性系」中相同、真空光速对谁都不变，时间和空间于是让了位。1908 年后他陆续任教，1914 年定居柏林，1915 年 11 月把「广义相对论与时空弯曲」的场方程交到普鲁士科学院；困扰天文学界半个世纪的水星近日点每世纪多出的 43 角秒，他的方程一次算中。1917 年他把同一套想法施于整个宇宙，为求静态解添上一个“宇宙学常数”，后来又自称这是他“一生中最大的失算”；同年他提出受激辐射，那是几十年后激光的理论地基。1919 年爱丁顿的日食观测证实星光确实被太阳偏折，让他一夜之间成为科学史上第一个全球性头版人物。1921 年度的诺贝尔奖（延迟到次年颁发）发给他的却是「光电效应实验」所揭示的光量子、而非相对论；有趣的是密立根当年正是想用精密实验证伪这条光量子方程，结果越测越服、反因此获了自己的诺奖。他终生不接受量子力学的概率诠释，与玻尔在历次索尔维会议正面交锋，“上帝不掷骰子”的诘问反而生出 EPR 悖论——几十年后它成了「波粒二象性」之外量子纠缠实验与量子信息学的起点。1933 年纳粹上台，他不再回德国，定居普林斯顿高等研究院；1939 年他签署致罗斯福的信促成了铀计划，晚年却为此懊悔。1955 年他在普林斯顿去世，留下“E=mc²”这一最简洁也最沉重的公式。
detailEn: In 1905, sitting at his desk as a third-class examiner in the Bern patent office, he produced four field-changing papers in a single year, plus a doctoral thesis: the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity, and the one extra page of mass-energy equivalence. All of it rested on two postulates — the laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame, and the speed of light in vacuum is the same for everyone — so space and time had to give way. After 1908 he taught in turn and settled in Berlin in 1914, handing the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy in November 1915; the 43 arc-seconds per century by which Mercury’s orbit overran Newtonian prediction, a puzzle for half an age, fell out of his equations at once. In 1917 he applied the same thinking to the whole universe, adding a “cosmological constant” to keep it static, and later called that his greatest blunder; that same year he proposed stimulated radiation, the theoretical ground of the laser decades on. Eddington’s 1919 eclipse expedition confirmed that starlight really bends around the Sun, and overnight he became the first scientist in history to make a global front page. The 1921 Nobel Prize (awarded the following year) honoured the light quantum revealed by the photoelectric effect, not relativity; tellingly, Millikan set out to refute that light-quantum equation by precision experiment and only grew more convinced the better it agreed, earning his own Nobel for the trouble. He never accepted the probability reading of quantum mechanics, clashed head-on with Bohr at successive Solvay Congresses, and his protest that “God does not play dice” generated the EPR argument, which decades later became the experimental starting point of entanglement and quantum information. When the Nazis came to power in 1933 he never returned to Germany and settled at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton; in 1939 he signed the letter to Roosevelt that launched the uranium project, and regretted it in his old age. He died at Princeton in 1955, leaving E=mc² as physics’ most compact and most fateful equation. He was born in Ulm in 1879 and had drifted through an unemployed year before the patent office saved him.

oneLiner: 统一电、磁、光，提出麦克斯韦方程组。
oneLinerEn: Unified electricity, magnetism and light via Maxwell's equations.
detail: 1831 年生于爱丁堡，恰好与爱因斯坦出生同年、只早了半个世纪出头——爱因斯坦书房里就挂着他的肖像。少年时他因把诗歌押韵迁移到数学上、写出最早的力多边形作图而得“数字缪斯”的诨名；爱丁堡与剑桥毕业后年纪轻轻便任教。1856 年为土星环作奖竞论文，他证明一环若是固体，会被土星潮汐力沿轨道撕碎，故只能是无数绕行的小颗粒——三百年后探测器照片证实他是对的。1860 年他给出气体分子速率分布律，把“温度”解释成分子平均动能、为「分子动理论」与统计力学奠基（后经玻尔兹曼推广成麦克斯韦—玻尔兹曼分布）。1861 年他从法拉第的力线出发补上“位移电流”，顺手算出由此产生的电磁波速度恰等于光速；1865 年给出电磁场的动力学理论，1873 年写成卷帙浩繁的《电学与磁学论》，第一次把电、磁、光统一成同一场里的波动——今天课本上那四个矢量方程，其实是赫维赛德与赫兹在 1880 年代把他原稿里二十多个分量式精简而成。他还是实验家：1861 年拍下世界上第一张永久性彩色照片（用红绿蓝三张滤色片，也由此奠定三原色原理），1871 年创建卡文迪许实验室并任首任主任，还精确测过气体黏度、手算过土星环的稳定性。1879 年他因病去世，年仅 48 岁，没能等到 1887 年赫兹在实验室里把他预言的那无形的波真的打出来——而无线电、电视、雷达、手机这一整条链，都从他补上的那一项“位移电流”开始。
detailEn: Born in Edinburgh in 1831, the very year of Einstein’s birth and only half a century ahead of him — Einstein kept his portrait on the study wall. As a boy he won the nickname “mathematical poet” for transporting the rhyme of verse into geometry and drawing force polygons early. After Edinburgh and Cambridge he was teaching as a young man. His 1856 prize essay on Saturn’s rings proved that if a ring were solid, Saturn’s tidal force would rend it along the orbit, so it must be a host of small orbiting particles — confirmed by probe photographs centuries later. In 1860 he gave the distribution of molecular speeds, reading “temperature” as the mean kinetic energy of molecules and founding the kinetic theory and statistical mechanics (later widened by Boltzmann into the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution). In 1861, starting from Faraday’s lines of force, he added the “displacement current” and found, almost as a by-product, that the resulting electromagnetic wave travelled at exactly the speed of light; the dynamical theory followed in 1865 and his bulky Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism in 1873, for the first time uniting electricity, magnetism and light as waves in one field — the four vector equations students memorise today are really Heaviside’s and Hertz’s compression of his twenty-odd component equations. He was an experimentalist too: in 1861 he took the world’s first permanent colour photograph (through red, green and blue filters, laying the ground of the three-primary theory), founded the Cavendish Laboratory in 1871 as its first professor, measured gas viscosity, and hand-computed the stability of Saturn’s rings. He died of illness in 1879, aged 48, never living to see Hertz actually generate those invisible waves he had predicted in 1887 — and the whole chain of radio, television, radar and mobile phones begins from the one term he added, the displacement current.

oneLiner: 原子量子化模型与哥本哈根诠释。
oneLinerEn: Quantized atomic model and the Copenhagen interpretation.
detail: 1885 年生于哥本哈根，1911 年到剑桥投在卢瑟福门下，正赶上原子被从“实心球”改成「原子的核式模型」。1913 年他连发三篇论原子结构的论文，把普朗克的量子硬装进卢瑟福的核式原子：规定电子只能待在若干条“定态”轨道上、角动量一份份量子化，跃迁时才发光，一举解释了「能级与氢原子光谱」里氢的谱线系、算出了里德伯常量与那条至今以他命名的玻尔半径；1918 年他又提出电子按壳层逐格填充的构造原理，给元素周期表找到了物理根基。这套模型只算得准氢、一到复杂原子就失灵，1926 年薛定谔方程一出即被取代——但“定态与跃迁”的内核留了下来。1920 年他创立哥本哈根理论物理研究所、1921 年正式落成，把它变成量子力学的教堂，1922 年因“原子结构与辐射”获诺贝尔奖。他与爱因斯坦在历次索尔维会议上就「波粒二象性」与概率诠释正面交锋，提出“互补原理”为哥本哈根诠释定调。1939 年，为躲避纳粹迫害而流亡的他与惠勒一起用液滴模型给出裂变的理论解释，并指出真正易裂变的是铀-235。1943 年他经鱼雷艇渡海逃出纳粹占领的丹麦，母亲后来死于集中营；他自己化名“尼古拉斯·贝克”先到伦敦、再赴洛斯阿拉莫斯参与曼哈顿计划，战后奔走于核武器的开放管控与不扩散。1950 年获英国功绩勋章，1962 年在哥本哈根去世；研究所今日改名尼尔斯·玻尔研究所，第 107 号元素以他命名为“玻尔”。他的弟弟哈拉尔是数学家，还拿过 1908 年伦敦奥运会的足球银牌——玻尔年轻时自己也是守门员。
detailEn: Born in Copenhagen in 1885, he went to Cambridge in 1911 to work under Rutherford just as the atom was being rewritten from a solid sphere into a nuclear model. In 1913 he fired off three papers on atomic structure, forcing Planck’s quantum into Rutherford’s nuclear atom: electrons may occupy only certain “stationary” orbits with angular momentum quantised in steps, and light is emitted only on a jump — explaining at a stroke the hydrogen spectral series and the Rydberg constant and computing the Bohr radius that still carries his name; in 1918 he added the building-up principle by which electrons fill shells, giving the periodic table a physical root. The model could only handle hydrogen and broke down for anything heavier, and Schrödinger’s equation supplanted it in 1926 — yet the core of stationary states and jumps survived. He founded the Copenhagen institute in 1920, opened in 1921, turned it into the cathedral of quantum mechanics, and won the 1922 Nobel Prize for atomic structure and radiation. With Einstein he clashed head-on at successive Solvay Congresses over wave-particle duality and the probability reading, and set the tone of the Copenhagen interpretation with his “complementarity.” In 1939 he and Wheeler, both refugees from Nazi persecution, turned the liquid-drop model into a theory of fission and pointed out that it is uranium-235 that fissures most easily. In 1943 he fled occupied Denmark by fishing boat across the sea; his mother later died in a camp. Under the alias “Nicholas Baker” he went first to London and then to Los Alamos on the Manhattan Project, and after the war campaigned for openness and control of nuclear weapons. He took the British Order of Merit in 1950 and died at Copenhagen in 1962; his institute now bears his name, and element 107, bohrium, was named for him. His brother Harald was a mathematician who won Olympic football silver in 1908 — Niels himself had been a goalkeeper in his youth.

oneLiner: 放射性研究先驱，首位两获诺贝尔奖的科学家。
oneLinerEn: Pioneer of radioactivity; first person to win two Nobel Prizes.
detail: 1867 年生于沙俄统治下的华沙，原名玛丽亚·斯克沃多夫斯卡。当时女子进不了大学，她与姐姐约定互相资助、先后去巴黎求学，此前先在乡下做了几年家庭教师；1891 年入索邦大学，以第一名的成绩读完物理、再修数学，1895 年与皮埃尔·居里结婚。她研究贝克勒尔发现的铀射线，用皮埃尔兄弟造的高灵敏度静电计逐份称量沥青铀矿的“射线强度”，发现钍也会自发放射，并造出“放射性”这个词；更惊人的是，某些矿石的放射远超其中铀所能解释，她据此断言里面藏着未知的强放射元素。1898 年她与皮埃尔先后宣布钋（以祖国波兰命名）与镭。为了证明镭确实是一种元素，他们在棚屋里把成吨的沥青铀矿渣一锅锅煮炼结晶，历时数年才从数吨残渣中提出约十分之一克纯镭盐、并测得镭的原子量约 225（今值 226）。1903 年诺贝尔物理学奖的提名起初只列了贝克勒尔与皮埃尔，经人提醒才补上她的名字——她由此成为第一位获诺贝尔奖的女性；1906 年皮埃尔在一场街头车祸中骤然丧生，她接过了他在索邦的讲席，成为该校第一位女教授。1911 年她因分离出纯镭并定出其原子量独得化学奖，至今仍是唯一横跨两科获奖的人；同年她与物理学家朗之万的私情风波被右翼媒体大肆渲染，几乎让法兰西科学院把她拒之门外。第一次世界大战期间，她把 X 光设备装上汽车、组织起约两百辆流动放射车奔赴前线，估计为上百万伤兵做了检查、避免了无数不必要的截肢。她的笔记本到今天仍带放射性，须存于铅盒、穿防护服才能查阅；1934 年她死于再生障碍性贫血，致病的就是她亲手发现、又日日随身携带的东西。她的女儿伊蕾娜与女婿约里奥 1935 年因人工放射性也拿了化学奖。1995 年，她与皮埃尔的遗骨移葬巴黎先贤祠，成为第一位凭自身成就入葬那里的女性。
detailEn: Born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw under Russian rule in 1867. Girls were shut out of university then, so she and her sister agreed to fund each other in turn and she went to Paris in 1891 after years as a rural governess; at the Sorbonne she took her physics degree first in the class, then added mathematics, and married Pierre Curie in 1895. Studying Becquerel’s uranium rays with the highly sensitive electrometer Pierre and his brother had built, she weighed the radiation of pitchblende sample by sample, found that thorium likewise gave off rays spontaneously, and coined the word “radioactivity.” More striking, some ores glowed far stronger than their uranium could account for, so she argued a potent unknown element lay hidden. She and Pierre announced polonium — named for her occupied homeland — and then radium in 1898. To prove radium was really an element, in a shed they boiled and crystallised ton after ton of pitchblende residue over several years, isolating about a tenth of a gram of pure radium salt from tons of waste and fixing radium’s atomic weight near 225 (modern value 226). The 1903 physics nomination listed only Becquerel and Pierre, and she was added only after someone pointed out the omission — becoming the first woman to win a Nobel. Pierre was killed outright in a street accident in 1906, and she took over his Sorbonne chair as the university’s first female professor. In 1911 she won the chemistry prize alone, for isolating pure radium and fixing its atomic weight, and she remains the only person to win Nobels in two sciences; that same year the press hounded her liaison with the physicist Langevin so savagely that the French Academy of Sciences very nearly refused to seat her. During the First World War she fitted cars with X-ray equipment and drove some two hundred mobile units to the front, thought to have examined over a million wounded soldiers and spared countless needless amputations. Her notebooks are still radioactive, kept in lead boxes and consulted in protective clothing; she died of aplastic anaemia in 1934, killed by what she had discovered and carried about daily. Her daughter Irène and son-in-law Joliot took the 1935 chemistry prize for artificial radioactivity. In 1995 her and Pierre’s remains were moved to the Paris Panthéon, she the first woman buried there on her own merits.

oneLiner: 近代实验物理与天文观测奠基人，惯性概念先驱。
oneLinerEn: Founder of modern experimental physics and observational astronomy; pioneer of inertia.
detail: 1564 年生于比萨（同年米开朗基罗辞世），1589 年起在比萨、继而在帕多瓦大学任教十八年。他真正的革命不在天上而在地上：相传比萨斜塔上两个铁球同时落地的演示多半出自学生的传闻，他做的是用「伽利略斜面实验」把自由下落“冲淡”到当时能测量的地步——让铜球沿光滑斜面滚下，用水钟（漏壶）计时，测得滚过的距离正比于所用时间的平方，即匀加速运动，再一路外推到竖直落体，得出落体与重量无关、只与时间平方相关的结论。他还把抛出的物体拆成水平匀速与竖直匀加速两笔，指出其轨迹是一条抛物线——这两件事合起来正是近代力学的起点。约 1602 年起他研究摆的等时性，萌生了用摆作钟表的念头。1609 年他听说荷兰人做出了能“望远”的镜筒，就自己磨镜片做到二十到三十倍，把镜口转向天空：看见月球满是环形山与沟壑、太阳有黑子、银河原是无数暗弱恒星挤在一起，还看到木星旁有四颗卫星在绕它转、金星竟像月亮一样有圆缺盈亏——“一切天体都绕地球”的地心说当场露了馅，「天体运动与开普勒定律」的日心图景则被这些观测撑了起来。1610 年他出版《星际信使》公布木星的四大卫星（故又称伽利略卫星），震动全欧。1616 年他被告诫不要坚持哥白尼学说，1632 年发表《关于两门世界体系的对话》为日心说辩护，半年内即被查禁，1633 年在宗教裁判所面前受审、被判终身软禁——相传他念完认罪词低声补了一句“可它确实在转动”。软禁中他写成的《关于两门新科学的对话》（1638 年）才是真正的力学奠基之作，而始终不肯放弃圆形轨道完美信念、拒绝开普勒椭圆的，也正是这个他。1642 年他在阿切特里去世；三百多年后的 1983 年，教廷正式承认当年对他的判决有误。1995 年抵达木星的探测器，以他的名字命名。
detailEn: Born in Pisa in 1564 (the year Michelangelo died), he taught from 1589 first at Pisa then for eighteen years at Padua. His real revolution was on the ground, not in the sky: the Leaning Tower demonstration with two balls landing together was probably a student’s tale, but what he truly did was dilute free fall along an inclined plane until it could be measured — rolling a bronze ball down a smooth groove, timing it with a water clock, and finding the distance run proportional to the square of the time, that is, uniform acceleration, then extrapolating all the way to a vertical drop and concluding that falling is independent of weight and governed by the square of time. He also split a thrown body into horizontal uniform motion and vertical uniform acceleration and showed its path is a parabola — and these two moves together were the start of modern mechanics. Around 1602 he studied the isochronism of the pendulum and conceived the pendulum clock. In 1609, hearing that the Dutch had made a tube that brought distant things near, he ground his own lenses to twenty or thirty powers and turned them skyward: he saw a Moon all craters and gorges, sunspots on the Sun, the Milky Way as a press of faint stars, four moons circling Jupiter, and Venus waxing and waning like our Moon — so “everything orbits the Earth” cracked open on the spot, while observations braced up the heliocentric picture of Kepler’s planetary motion. His Sidereal Messenger of 1610 announced the four satellites of Jupiter (hence Galilean moons) and shook all Europe. Warned in 1616 not to hold to Copernicus, he published his Dialogue on the Two Chief World Systems in 1632 to defend the heliocentric view; within six months it was banned, and in 1633 he stood before the Inquisition and was sentenced to house arrest for life — said to have muttered, after recanting, “and yet it moves.” The Two New Sciences he wrote under confinement (1638) is the true founding text of mechanics, and it was this same man who clung to perfect circular orbits and refused Kepler’s ellipses. He died at Arcetri in 1642; more than three centuries later, in 1983, the Church formally acknowledged the old verdict against him had been wrong. The probe that reached Jupiter in 1995 was named for him.

oneLiner: 发现电磁感应，奠定电力工业基础。
oneLinerEn: Discovered electromagnetic induction, foundation of the electrical industry.
detail: 1791 年生于伦敦近郊一个铁匠贫家，正规教育只到识字与初级算术，代数都使他为难——他后来全部的物理直觉几乎不借助数学。十二三岁进书肆当装订学徒，五年里把经手的书一本本读过去；1812 年他花掉几乎整周工钱买票去听戴维的公开讲座，把讲稿整理成厚厚的笔记呈上去自荐，1813 年终于得戴维收作助手（起初只肯做杂役），还随戴维欧游数年大开眼界。1820 年奥斯特发现电流能使磁针偏转，次年法拉第就做出让导线绕着磁极不停旋转的装置——“电磁旋转”，把电能变成持续的机械运动，是电动机的祖先，当时却被同行讥为“无用的把戏”。1831 年他反过来追问“磁能否生电”，用两个线圈发现只有在一个通电或断电的瞬间、另一个里才闪过一股电流，据此确立「电磁感应」定律与感应电流方向的规律，造出最早的感应圆盘，让电力第一次成为可以源源不断产生的东西——今天整座电力工业的原理由此而起。1833 年起他给出电解定律，把电与化学计量定量地连起来，“电极”“离子”“阳极”“阴极”这些词是惠威尔为他造的；后人把电解一摩尔单价离子所需的电量记作法拉第常数，约 9.65×10⁴ 库仑每摩尔，恰等于元电荷乘以阿伏伽德罗常数。他数学近乎为零，却坚持用“力线”去想象空间本身被电场与磁场充满，把物理学从超距作用里解放出来——麦克斯韦说自己的方程不过是给法拉第的思想作的翻译，爱因斯坦把场论的源头也记在他名下。1845 年他发现有些材料会被磁场排斥（抗磁性），又发现让偏振光穿过被磁化的玻璃时振动面会旋转——“法拉第效应”，第一次把光与电磁牵连在一起。1855 年他拒绝为克里米亚战争研制毒气。1825 年他创办的皇家研究所圣诞讲座延续至今，他自己一生却两次婉拒封爵、也拒绝出任皇家学会会长（因信仰不肯宣誓）。1867 年他安详离世，只想长眠于海格特那块再普通不过的墓里。
detailEn: Born in 1791 to a poor blacksmith’s family on the edge of London, his formal schooling stopped at reading and elementary arithmetic, and algebra itself was a struggle — nearly all his later physical intuition ran without mathematics. Apprenticed at twelve or thirteen to a bookbinder, he read his way through the volumes that crossed his bench for five years; in 1812 he spent almost a week’s wages on a ticket to Davy’s public lectures, bound his notes into a thick volume and offered them as a recommendation, and in 1813 finally got taken on by Davy as an assistant (glad at first even to do menial work), touring Europe with him for several years and seeing a great deal. After Oersted found in 1820 that a current deflects a compass needle, Faraday the very next year built a device that spun a wire endlessly around a magnetic pole — “electromagnetic rotation,” turning electricity into continuous motion, the ancestry of the motor, then mocked by colleagues as a useless trick. In 1831 he asked the reverse, can magnetism make electricity, and with two coils found that only in the instant a current is started or stopped does a flash of current jump in the other, fixing the law of electromagnetic induction and the rule for its direction and building the earliest induction disc — the first time electricity could be made to flow in a stream, the principle on which the whole electrical industry stands. From 1833 he gave the laws of electrolysis, tying electricity to chemical amounts with numbers, and the words electrode, ion, anode and cathode were coined for him by Whewell; the charge needed to electrolyse one mole of a singly charged ion is still called the faraday, about 9.65×10⁴ coulombs per mole, exactly the elementary charge times the Avogadro constant. Almost without mathematics, he insisted on lines of force filling space itself, freeing physics from action at a distance — Maxwell called his own equations a translation of Faraday’s ideas, and Einstein traced field theory back to him. In 1845 he found that some materials are repelled by a magnet (diamagnetism), and that passing polarised light through magnetised glass turns its plane of vibration — the Faraday effect, the first to link light and electromagnetism. In 1855 he refused to help design chemical weapons for the Crimean War. The Royal Institution Christmas Lectures he founded in 1825 run to this day, though he twice declined a knighthood and refused the presidency of the Royal Society (his faith would not let him swear the oath). He died peacefully in 1867, asking only to lie in an unremarkable grave at Highgate.

oneLiner: 提出行星运动三定律，揭示天体运行规律。
oneLinerEn: Formulated the three laws of planetary motion.
detail: 1571 年生于德国的小城魏尔德，幼年一场天花让他视力受损、体弱多病，却把他推向天文。1596 年他写出《宇宙的奥秘》，用五个正多面体层层嵌套去解释当时已知六颗行星的轨道间距——这个模型后来被他自己推翻，但那份“宇宙背后必有一套可算的数学秩序”的执念是对的，也正是它引来第谷的注意。1600 年他赴布拉格与第谷合作，一年后第谷去世、留下一辈子肉眼观测的数据，精度达一到两角分，是望远镜之前史上最准的一份。为火星这颗第谷指定的“硬骨头”，他苦战经年：圆的轨道始终与观测差着约 8 角分，他不肯把这当成误差抹平，终于承认轨道是椭圆，1609 年出版《新天文学》公布前两大定律——轨道是以太阳为一个焦点的椭圆（火星偏心率约 0.093）、行星与太阳连线在相等时间里扫过相等的面积，于是行星近时快、远时慢。第二条面积定律用今天的话说，本质上正是角动量守恒在天幕上的投影。1619 年他在《世界的和谐》里给出第三定律：各行星公转周期的平方正比于其轨道半长轴的立方，从此六条轨道不再是六件孤立的事，而被串成一个可算的体系——这正是四十年后牛顿「万有引力定律」最直接的经验地基。他的动机并不“现代”：他相信有一种从太阳发出、随距离减弱并扫动行星的力（那是引力观念的前身），也着迷于数字与几何的和谐。他还是光学先驱：1604 年正确解释了近视与远视的成因、说明小孔成像与光线如何落在视网膜上，并改进出用两片凸透镜的开普勒式望远镜。1615 年母亲被控行巫术、被囚十四个月，他放下研究为她辩护，花六年打赢官司；1627 年凭第谷数据编成《鲁道夫星表》、把行星位置算到约两角分精度，却因战乱迟迟未能印行。1630 年，他为向雇主讨要拖欠多年的薪俸奔赴雷根斯堡，病逝途中，终年五十九岁。他一生清贫动荡，却在天上为人类理清了行星的舞步。
detailEn: Born in 1571 in the small German town of Weil der Stadt, a childhood attack of smallpox left him frail and short-sighted yet pushed him toward the sky. In 1596 he published the Cosmographic Mystery, nesting the five regular solids to explain the spacings of the six then-known planetary orbits — a model he later overthrew himself, but his faith that a computable mathematical order must lie behind the cosmos was right, and it drew Tycho’s attention. In 1600 he went to Prague to work with Tycho, who died the next year leaving a lifetime of naked-eye data accurate to one or two arc-minutes, the best before the telescope. Over the planet Tycho had assigned him, the tough nut of Mars, he laboured for years: a circular orbit never matched the observations by about eight arc-minutes, and instead of smoothing that off as error he conceded the orbit is an ellipse, publishing the New Astronomy in 1609 with the first two laws — the orbit is an ellipse with the Sun at one focus (Mars’ eccentricity is about 0.093), and the line joining planet to Sun sweeps equal areas in equal times, so a planet speeds up near the Sun and slows far away; that equal-areas law, in modern words, is essentially the conservation of angular momentum projected onto the sky. In 1619, in The Harmony of the Worlds, he gave the third law: the squares of the periods are proportional to the cubes of the orbits’ semi-major axes, so the six orbits ceased to be six isolated facts and were strung into one computable system — the most direct empirical foundation of Newton’s universal gravitation forty years on. His motives were not “modern”: he believed in a force issuing from the Sun, weakening with distance and sweeping the planets along, a precursor of gravitation, and he was bewitched by the harmony of number and geometry. He was also an optical pioneer: in 1604 he correctly explained near- and farsightedness, how a pinhole forms an image and how light falls on the retina, and improved the telescope into the Keplerian form with two convex lenses. In 1615 his mother was charged with witchcraft and held fourteen months; he set aside his work and spent six years winning her defence. In 1627 he compiled the Rudolphine Tables from Tycho’s data, placing the planets to about two arc-minutes, but war delayed their printing. In 1630, travelling to Regensburg to collect a salary withheld from him for years, he fell ill and died on the road, aged fifty-nine. He lived poor and restless, yet up in the sky he set the planets’ dance in order for humankind.

oneLiner: 提出能量量子化，开创量子理论。
oneLinerEn: Proposed energy quantization, launching quantum theory.
detail: 1900 年 10 月他写出黑体辐射公式，12 月 14 日他被迫承认能量只能一份一份地发射与吸收，这一天通常被当作量子理论的生日。他自称那是「绝望之举」，此后十几年一直想把它塞回经典框架；他拟合出的 h 约 6.55×10⁻³⁴ J·s，与今天的 6.626 只差约百分之一。他本人保守，1913 年推荐爱因斯坦进普鲁士科学院时特意补了一句：他偶尔会跑得太远，比如光量子假说。1918 年的诺贝尔奖延迟到次年颁发。纳粹年代他没有离德，1945 年儿子因涉刺杀希特勒案被处决；两年后他去世，1948 年那个学会以他的名字重命名。
detailEn: In October 1900 he wrote down the black-body formula; on 14 December he conceded that energy is emitted and absorbed only in packets, a date now taken as the birthday of quantum theory. He called it an act of desperation and spent the next decade trying to push it back into classical physics. His value of h, about 6.55×10⁻³⁴ J·s, misses today's 6.626 by roughly one per cent. Politically conservative, he nominated Einstein to the Prussian Academy in 1913 with the caveat that he sometimes overshoots the mark, as with the light quantum. His 1918 Nobel Prize was awarded a year late. He stayed in Germany through Nazism, and in 1945 his son was executed for the plot against Hitler. He died two years later; in 1948 the learned society was renamed for him.

oneLiner: 首次实验证实电磁波存在。
oneLinerEn: First experimentally confirmed electromagnetic waves.
detail: 1857 年生于汉堡一个法学世家，起初在德累斯顿学工程（曾以弹性体模拟晶体光学的各向异性，那份“赫兹接触”的力学分析至今是接触问题的起点），后转投物理、进柏林大学师从亥姆霍兹。老师给他出了道题：去证明麦克斯韦预言的那些“电磁波”真的存在。1887 至 1888 年，他在卡尔斯鲁厄理工的实验室里，用感应线圈激励一对中间留了小间隙的铜棒（偶极振子）当发射器，再以一个同样留缝的开环当接收器——当发送端火花一闪，接收环对面的小缝里竟也跳出了微弱的火花：波真的收到了。他一步步测出这种波会被金属板反射、被石蜡大棱镜折射、是横波、并会叠成驻波，再由测得的波长与频率算出它的速度约 3×10⁸ 米每秒、与光速吻合——麦克斯韦赢了，光从此被并成电磁波谱里可见的那一小段，无线电、电视、雷达、手机整条链都从这对简陋的火花隙起步。有意思的是，就在同一年他发现一束紫外光照到接收电极上、会让火花更容易跳起来，这是「光电效应实验」最早的一条观测记录，其解释要等爱因斯坦 1905 年接手、并据「波粒二象性」的光量子一举道破。可他对自己造出的波和这道光电现象都提不起应用兴趣，说这一切“不过是证明麦克斯韦是对的”，也由此留下科技史上最著名的失算之一：把无线电拱手让给了后来的马可尼与波波夫。他一生纯粹做基础物理，还研究过阴极射线的本性（误以为它能穿透薄金属、偏向波动说，与勒纳德的粒子说相持，后来才厘清），并精确测过接触起电。1894 年他因血液感染（败血症）骤然离世，年仅 36 岁。为了纪念他，频率的单位——每秒一次振动——被命名为“赫兹”，直到 1960 年才由国际计量大会正式并入国际单位制。
detailEn: Born in Hamburg in 1857 into a family of jurists, he first studied engineering in Dresden (modelling the anisotropy of crystal optics with elastic bodies, and that “Hertzian contact” analysis of stress is still the starting point of contact problems), then turned to physics and went to the University of Berlin under Helmholtz. His teacher set him a task: go prove that the electromagnetic waves Maxwell predicted really exist. In 1887–1888, in the laboratory at Karlsruhe, he drove a pair of copper rods with a small gap in the middle — a dipole oscillator — as a transmitter with an induction coil, and caught the wave with an open ring that likewise had a gap: when a spark flashed at the sender, a faint spark leapt across the far side of the receiving ring too. The wave had been received. Step by step he showed it is reflected by metal sheets, refracted by a giant paraffin prism, is a transverse wave, and stacks into standing waves; from the measured wavelength and frequency he computed its speed at about 3×10⁸ metres per second, matching the speed of light — Maxwell had won, light was folded into the visible sliver of the electromagnetic spectrum, and the whole chain of radio, television, radar and mobile phones begins from those two crude spark gaps. Curiously, that same year he noticed that ultraviolet light falling on the receiving electrode made the spark jump more readily — the first recorded observation of the photoelectric effect, left for Einstein to explain in 1905 with the light quantum and wave-particle duality. Yet he took no interest in applications for either the waves or the photoelectric phenomenon, calling all of it “just a proof that Maxwell was right,” and so handed down one of the most famous miscalculations in the history of technology: radio went to Marconi and Popov, who came after. He spent his life on pure physics, also probing the nature of cathode rays (wrongly leaning toward the wave view because he thought they passed through thin metal, at odds with Lenard’s particle view, cleared up only later) and measuring contact electrification precisely. In 1894 he died suddenly of a blood infection, sepsis, at only 36. In his honour the unit of frequency — one vibration per second — was named the hertz, though it was only formally folded into the SI by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1960.

oneLiner: α 粒子散射确立原子的核式结构，首次实现人工核转变。
oneLinerEn: Alpha scattering gave the nuclear atom; first artificial transmutation of an element.
detail: 新西兰农场出身，1895 年靠卡文迪许奖学金进剑桥，1898 年到蒙特利尔任讲席。在加拿大他与索迪建立起衰变理论、提出半衰期概念，主张放射性就是元素在自发转变——1908 年的化学奖就发给了这项工作，他自嘲毕生把别人的元素变来变去，却没把自己从物理学家变成化学家。1909 年盖革与马斯登在他手下用 α 粒子轰金箔，约八千个里有一个被原路反弹回来；1911 年他据此把原子改成「中心一个很小很重的核，四周几乎全空」。1917 年他用 α 轰氮，第一次人工把一种元素变成另一种，并从飞出的粒子中认出质子；1920 年他已预言中子存在，1932 年由查德威克找到。他执掌卡文迪许实验室后，学生与共事者里出了十多位诺贝尔奖得主。他也留下两个著名失算：核式原子按经典电动力学本该在一瞬间坍缩，他把这个问题留给了玻尔；1933 年他公开断言从原子蜕变中取能「不过是无稽之谈」，四年后裂变被证实。
detailEn: He grew up on a New Zealand farm, reached Cambridge in 1895 on a Cavendish scholarship and took a chair in Montreal in 1898. There, with Soddy, he built the theory of radioactive decay, named the half-life and insisted that radioactivity was elements transforming into other elements — the work that brought him the 1908 chemistry prize, which he took as a joke at his own expense: he had spent his life transmuting other people's elements without ever turning himself from a physicist into a chemist. In 1909 Geiger and Marsden, working under him, fired alpha particles at gold foil and found that about one in eight thousand came straight back, so in 1911 he rebuilt the atom as a tiny heavy nucleus inside a mostly empty volume. In 1917 the alpha bombardment of nitrogen gave the first artificial transmutation of one element into another, and he identified the proton among the particles flying out. He had forecast the neutron in 1920; Chadwick found it in 1932. As head of the Cavendish, more than ten Nobel laureates passed through his students and collaborators. His two famous misses: a nuclear atom should collapse classically in an instant, a problem he handed on to Bohr; and in 1933 he declared that any power obtainable from the transmutation of atoms was moonshine, four years before fission was proved.

oneLiner: 发现电子：阴极射线是带比荷的微粒，原子并非不可再分。
oneLinerEn: Discovered the electron: cathode rays are particles with a measurable charge ratio.
detail: 1884 年，27 岁的他当上卡文迪许教授，主持这间实验室三十多年，直到 1919 年由卢瑟福来接。1897 年他在阴极射线管里分别用磁场与电场把它偏转，测得这种「微体」的比荷约为氢离子的 1800 倍，据此宣布原子并非不可分；他叫它 corpuscle，后来被命名为电子，1906 年他因气体导电的研究获诺贝尔奖。1904 年他给出「葡萄干布丁」模型：正电荷铺满整个球、电子嵌在其中。这个模型被学生的学生的散射实验推翻，可他追问的「正电荷在原子中如何分布」恰恰是此后所有散射实验真正要测的东西。他还是质谱的先驱：1912 年让带正电的射线穿过交叉的电场与磁场，在底片上按荷质比分出抛物线束，其中氖有一条位置偏重的谱迹，即氖-22——同位素的实验证据比阿斯顿的仪器更早。局限同样明确：他只测到 e/m，电荷值要等密立根；他晚年认定电子是以太里的涡环，把原子结构引向思辨而非测量。他与儿子分别在 1906 与 1937 年因「电子是粒子」和「电子会衍射」获奖，正是同一物体的两张脸。
detailEn: He was made Cavendish professor in 1884 at the age of 27 and ran the laboratory for more than thirty years, until Rutherford came to take it over in 1919. In 1897 he deflected cathode rays separately with magnetic and electric fields and found their charge-to-mass ratio about 1800 times that of the hydrogen ion, concluding that the atom was not divisible; he called them corpuscles and the name that stuck was the electron, while his work on conduction in gases earned him the 1906 physics prize. His 1904 plum-pudding atom spread positive charge through the whole sphere with electrons set inside it. The model fell to a scattering experiment run by a student's student, yet the question he was asking — how is positive charge distributed inside an atom — is exactly what scattering experiments still measure. He also founded mass spectrometry: in 1912 his positively charged rays passed crossed fields and separated on a photographic plate into parabolas by charge-to-mass ratio, and one neon trace sat unmistakably heavy, neon-22, evidence for isotopes before Aston's instrument. His limits match his successes: he measured only e/m, leaving the charge itself to Millikan, and in later life he argued that corpuscles were vortex rings in the ether, steering atomic structure towards speculation rather than measurement. He and his son shared the 1906 and 1937 prizes for the electron as a particle and the electron as a wave, two faces of one object.

oneLiner: 油滴实验测出元电荷，并精确验证爱因斯坦的光电方程。
oneLinerEn: The oil-drop charge of the electron and a precision test of Einstein's photoelectric equation.
detail: 1909 年起他把水滴换成不易蒸发的油滴，用喷雾器让油雾穿过小孔缓缓落下，靠两块平行板间的电场把某一滴悬停或倒退，反复测它的电荷，得出 e 约 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ 库仑，把「电荷只能一份一份地出现」钉成实验事实；同一个数字还能反推阿伏伽德罗常量、普朗克常量与电子质量。1914 到 1916 年他做了第二件事：用单色光照射碱金属、测截止电压随频率的变化，检验爱因斯坦 1905 年那条光量子方程。他本自认是来证伪的，量出的直线斜率却正好是普朗克常量，1916 年他承认这方程「与我们现在持有的任何图像都无法调和，却已被实验完全证实」。1923 年诺贝尔奖发给了这两项工作。争议也长在同一张表上：1970 年代科学史家霍尔顿指出，他发表油滴数据时略去了若干不合期望的滴，「失踪数据」之争至今未息——也有学者为他辩护，说被剔掉的每一滴都能指出蒸发或气流干扰。他晚年坚持宇宙线是来自恒星的原始光、宇宙是稳态的，这一条被超新星起源说驳倒。
detailEn: From 1909 he swapped water for oil, which evaporates far less, sprayed single drops through a pinhole and used the field between two plates to hold one drop still or drive it back, measuring its charge again and again until the result pinned the elementary charge near 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ coulomb and made 'charge comes only in whole units' an experimental fact. The same number let him back out Avogadro's constant, Planck's constant and the mass of the electron. Then, from 1914 to 1916, he did a second job: shining monochromatic light on alkali metals and measuring stopping voltage against frequency to test Einstein's 1905 light-quantum equation. He expected to refute it; the slope of his line was Planck's constant, and in 1916 he conceded that the equation, which could not be reconciled with any picture then possessed, had nevertheless been completely justified by experiment. The 1923 Nobel Prize covered both pieces of work. The reproach grew from the same table of numbers: in the 1970s the historian Holton showed that drops disagreeing with his conclusion had been left out of the published data, and the case of the missing drops is still argued, other historians defending each omission as a drop with identifiable evaporation or air disturbance. In his later years he insisted that cosmic rays were pristine light from the stars and that the universe was steady, a position the supernova origin of cosmic rays defeated.

oneLiner: 扭秤称量地球，电学手稿提前一个世纪，判定氢气与水。
oneLinerEn: Weighed the Earth with a torsion balance, left electrical manuscripts a century ahead, settled hydrogen and water.
detail: 他继承了米歇尔留下的装置：一根轻质横杆两端各吊一只小球，用细丝悬起，再把两只约 350 磅的大铅球搬到杆的两侧——大球吸引小球，把悬丝扭过一个极小的角度，而这正是整个实验的全部难点。1798 年，他 67 岁，测出地球平均密度约为水的 5.48 倍（今天公认 5.51），误差不到百分之二。当时这成果并不被说成「测出了万有引力常量」——G 要到十九世纪后半才被直接给出——而被说成「称量地球」。他的电学手稿写于 1771 年，用一组莱顿瓶证明电力服从平方反比，又做出电荷全落在导体外表面的「冰桶」实验，比普里斯特利的提示更进一步、比库仑的扭秤早十四年，却压着不发；一百年后麦克斯韦在 1879 年把这些手稿编印成册，人们才发现他几乎把电学提前想完。化学上他分离出「可燃空气」即氢、判定它是单质，1784 年让氢在空气中爆鸣生成水，从而把水从元素表上划掉。他孤僻到与女仆用字条交谈、把住宅一侧的楼梯封起来以免撞到来客，大量成果锁在抽屉里，好些优先权要等手稿被翻出来才归还给他。
detailEn: He inherited the apparatus John Michell had designed: a light horizontal rod with a small ball at each end, suspended on a fine thread, with two lead balls of some 350 pounds moved up beside it. The big balls tugged the small ones and twisted the thread through an angle so tiny that measuring it was the entire difficulty. In 1798, aged 67, he found the mean density of the Earth at 5.48 times that of water, against today's accepted 5.51, a miss of under two per cent. His contemporaries did not describe this as measuring the gravitational constant, which waited for the later nineteenth century, but as weighing the world. His electrical manuscripts of 1771 used a bank of Leyden jars to show that electric force falls off as the inverse square of distance, and proved that charge resides entirely on the outer surface of a conductor — the ice-pail experiment — going further than Priestley's hint and anticipating Coulomb's torsion balance by fourteen years, all of it unpublished; it took Maxwell's 1879 edition of the papers for people to realise that he had thought through most of electricity. In chemistry he isolated inflammable air, judged hydrogen to be a simple substance, and in 1784 exploded it in air to water, removing water from the list of elements. He was unsociable to the point of talking to his housekeeper by note and walling off one staircase of his house to avoid meeting callers, and so much of his work stayed in drawers that several priorities were only returned to him when the manuscripts were read out decades later.

term: 詹姆斯·普雷斯科特·焦耳
oneLiner: 热功当量的定量测量与焦耳定律，奠定能量守恒的实验根基。
oneLinerEn: Measured the mechanical equivalent of heat and the heating law of currents; grounded energy conservation.
detail: 他是索尔福德啤酒厂主的儿子，因体弱在家念书，16 岁进了道尔顿的课堂。1840 年他 22 岁发表电流发热定律——发热正比于电流的平方与电阻，比楞次的独立发现早三年。1843 到 1850 年他把「功变成热」做成可重复的定量实验：让下落的重物带动浸在水里的叶轮转，再量水暖了多少。整个四十年代他测得把一磅水升高 1°F 大约要八百多英尺·磅的功，也就是说十磅的重物得下落八十多英尺才够，他因此打趣说自己需要一个八十英尺高的房间；1878 年他最好的数值与今天的 778 已差不到百分之一。1847 年他在英国科学促进会宣读这结果，同年亥姆霍兹从另一个入口发表能量守恒；而在「热不是物质而是运动」这一点上，焦耳坚持得更早也更硬——他干脆不接受热质说。他与汤姆孙（后来的开尔文勋爵）合作量出节流会降温的焦耳-汤姆孙效应，为液化气体开了路。局限也在这儿：他只信机械运动的图像，对场与势能这些新工具并不热心；以他名字命名的能量单位到十九世纪末才定下、1948 年列入国际单位制。
detailEn: The son of a Salford brewer, too frail for school he was taught at home and at 16 became one of Dalton's pupils. In 1840, aged 22, he published the law that a current's heating goes as the square of the current times the resistance, three years before Lenz reached it independently. From 1843 to 1850 he made the turning of work into heat a repeatable number: falling weights drove paddles immersed in water and he measured how much warmer the water came out. Through the 1840s the eight-hundred-odd foot-pounds he measured to raise a pound of water by a Fahrenheit degree meant a ten-pound weight falling more than eighty feet, which is why he joked that he required an eighty-foot room; by 1878 his best value was within a per cent of today's 778. He read the result to the British Association in 1847, the same year Helmholtz published conservation of energy from another direction, and on the point that heat is not a substance but motion Joule had been earlier and more stubborn, since he would not accept the caloric theory at all. With William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin, he measured the cooling of throttled gases — the Joule-Thomson effect that opened the road to liquefying gases. His limit lay in the same place: he trusted pictures of mechanical motion and took little interest in fields and potential energy, and the energy unit bearing his name was only settled at the end of the nineteenth century before entering SI in 1948.

oneLiner: 矩阵力学与不确定性原理，量子力学的奠基者之一。
oneLinerEn: Matrix mechanics and the uncertainty principle; a founder of quantum mechanics.
detail: 1925 年夏他到黑尔戈兰岛养花粉症，在那里算出一套不用电子轨道、只让可观测的谱线与强度彼此相乘的量子力学；回哥廷根后与玻恩、约尔当一起把它写成三人论文。不到一年薛定谔的波动力学出现，狄拉克证明两者本是同一个理论。1926 到 1927 年他与玻尔反复争「这套算符究竟说了什么」，1927 年给出测不准关系：位置测得越准，动量就越模糊，两者不确定度的乘积不小于普朗克常量的量级——严格的 Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2 是肯纳德同年补出来的。1932 年他因「创立量子力学——其应用之一引出了氢的两种形态的发现」获诺贝尔奖，颁奖词把奖项钉在具体可验的成果上；纳粹兴起后他却被攻击搞「犹太物理学」，1937 年遭官方调查，他公开表态效忠、承诺留在德国才平息。1941 年他去哥本哈根拜访玻尔，那次谈话的动机至今无定论，被弗莱恩写成戏剧《哥本哈根》；战后他们在农场庄园被拘留期间的录音显示，德国铀计划的成员既没有造弹的思路，也缺关键工艺。他后半生的另一条线在原子核上：与伊凡年科各自给出质子-中子的核模型，提出同位旋与核子间的交换力，又把 S 矩阵当作绕开波函数的思路留给强相互作用物理。
detailEn: In the summer of 1925 he went to the island of Helgoland to recover from hay fever and there worked out a quantum mechanics that used no electron orbits at all, only arrays of observable spectral lines and intensities that multiplied one another; back in Göttingen, Born and Jordan turned it into the three-man paper. Within a year Schrödinger's wave mechanics appeared and Dirac showed the two were the same theory. From 1926 he argued with Bohr over what the formalism actually said, and in 1927 he published the uncertainty relation — the sharper the position, the blurrer the momentum, with the product of the two spreads no smaller than the scale of Planck's constant, while the exact bound of Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2 was supplied by Kennard the same year. His 1932 Nobel Prize for the creation of quantum mechanics cited, in its official wording, the application that had led to the discovery of the allotropic forms of hydrogen — a prize pinned to a checkable result. After 1933 the Nazis' acolytes denounced him for practising Jewish physics and an official inquiry followed in 1937; he survived it only by publicly pledging to stay in Germany. His 1941 visit to Bohr in Copenhagen left a conversation whose motive is still unsettled — Frayn made a play of it — and the recordings made while he and his colleagues were detained at Farm Hall after the war show that the German uranium project had neither a bomb design nor the missing industrial steps. His later work ran on another track: with Ivanenko he gave the nucleus its proton-neutron picture, he introduced isotope spin and exchange forces between nucleons, and he proposed the S-matrix as a way around wave functions that strong-interaction physics later took up.

oneLiner: 波动力学与那只猫，用一条方程换掉了电子轨道。
oneLinerEn: Wave mechanics and that cat: one equation in place of electron orbits.
detail: 1925 年冬他在苏黎世读到德布罗意的物质波论文，想既然电子是波就该有波动方程，1926 年连发四篇，把方程写成 iħ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ 的本征值形式，氢原子能级一次算出，不必再往轨道上硬贴量子化条件；他在第三篇里顺手演示了这套算法与海森堡的矩阵力学等价，狄拉克与冯·诺伊曼随后把它抬成一般定理。分歧在 ψ 是什么：他主张电荷真的摊成了波、波包就是粒子，海森堡回信算给他看波包会自己散开，玻恩再把 |ψ|² 读成概率密度，三人这场架打成今天教科书的第一道选择题。1933 年他与狄拉克共享诺贝尔奖，颁奖词是「原子理论的新生产形式」。1938 年德奥合并后他在维也纳待不下去，先到罗马与牛津，1940 年受邀到都柏林高等研究院主持理论物理学部；1944 年出版的《生命是什么？》里那句「生命以负熵为食」与对非周期性分子的推想，把一批物理学家推向了分子生物学。同年他为了奚落哥本哈根诠释，借爱因斯坦来信里的放射性原子设想了一只又死又活的猫，也在这篇文章里首次写下「纠缠」一词。1956 年他回维也纳主持理论物理研究所，1961 年 1 月 4 日在阿尔特巴赫去世；他没能赢下那场诠释之争，可他留下的纠缠在 1964 年贝尔不等式与八十年代的实验之后，从哲学辩论变成了实验室里可用的资源。
detailEn: In the winter of 1925, in Zurich, he read de Broglie's paper on matter waves and asked why a particle that is a wave should not obey a wave equation; four papers in 1926 put it in the eigenvalue form iħ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ and gave the hydrogen levels in one stroke, with no quantum condition pinned onto orbits afterwards. In the third of them he showed his algorithm reproduced Heisenberg's matrix mechanics, a link Dirac and von Neumann later raised to a general theorem. The quarrel was over what ψ is: he insisted the charge really was smeared into a wave and the wave packet was the particle, Heisenberg wrote back with arithmetic showing packets spread on their own, and Born read |ψ|² as a probability density — the three-way disagreement is still the first multiple-choice question in every textbook. He shared the 1933 Nobel Prize with Dirac, cited for new productive forms of atomic theory. After the 1938 Anschluss Vienna became impossible: Rome and Oxford first, then from 1940 the school of theoretical physics of the Dublin Institute, where his 1944 book What Is Life? argued that life feeds on negative entropy and guessed at an aperiodic molecule — a short book that pushed a generation of physicists into molecular biology. The same year, needling the Copenhagen reading with a radioactive atom taken from Einstein's letters to him, he described a cat both dead and alive and coined the word entanglement. He went back to Vienna in 1956 to run the institute's theoretical physics chair and died at Alpbach on 4 January 1961. He lost the interpretation argument; the entanglement he left behind, after Bell's 1964 inequality and the experiments of the 1980s, became a resource laboratories can actually spend.

oneLiner: 不相容原理与中微子预言，量子力学最锋利的批评者。
oneLinerEn: The exclusion principle and the neutrino forecast; quantum mechanics' sharpest critic.
detail: 1921 年他 21 岁在慕尼黑拿博士学位，导师索末菲把《数学百科全书》的相对论词条交给这个研究生写，这篇厚重的综述此后重印不辍，爱因斯坦读后说很难相信作者是个刚答辩的年轻人。1924 年他给电子加了一个「经典图像里没有对应物的双值量子数」，1925 年 1 月据此发表不相容原理：同一个原子中不能有两个电子处于完全相同的状态，电子壳层与元素周期表从此有力学根据，白矮星为何不塌也归到这条原理；几个月后乌伦贝克与高兹米特才把那个量子数叫作自旋，而泡利起初并不认账，直到 1927 年用自己的泡利矩阵把它写进理论。1930 年 12 月他寄给图宾格一场放射学会议一封信，开头是「亲爱的放射性先生女士们」，提议让一种极轻、极难捕获的中性粒子带走 β 衰变里失踪的能量与角动量；1932 年查德威克发现中子之后，费米给这粒子定名中微子，1933 年的 β 衰变理论干脆拿它当地基，弱相互作用由此开张。1935 年起他任苏黎世联邦理工理论物理教授，二战的几年在美国讲学，1946 年回苏黎世。1940 年他证明自旋与统计必须绑定（整数自旋相拥、半整数自排斥），1945 年诺贝尔奖只提一件事：发现不相容原理。他与爱因斯坦就量子力学是否完备通信辩论了三十年，是少数敢当面驳倒海森堡与玻尔的人；荣格给他分析了上千个梦，两人想弄清楚物质与心灵会不会有同一副底子。他的刻薄成了行话——一份稿子的评语是「这连错误都算不上」；1931 年哥廷根一台光谱仪在实验中炸毁，同事们说那是因为泡利在场，从此这类事故叫「泡利效应」。1958 年 12 月 15 日他因胰腺癌在苏黎世去世，58 岁。
detailEn: He took his Munich doctorate in 1921 at twenty-one, and Sommerfeld handed this graduate student the relativity article for the Encyklopädie der mathematischen Wissenschaften: an authoritative article that stayed in print for decades and that Einstein said he could hardly believe came from someone who had just defended a thesis. In 1924 he added to the electron a two-valued quantum number with no classical counterpart, and in January 1925 published the exclusion principle — no two electrons in an atom may share one complete state — which gave the shells and the whole periodic table a mechanical basis, and later a reason why white dwarfs hold themselves up. Uhlenbeck and Goudsmit named that number spin only months after him, and Pauli would not accept it until he had written it into his own theory with his matrices in 1927. In December 1930 he mailed a note to a radiology meeting in Tübingen headed Dear radioactive ladies and gentlemen, proposing an almost massless, almost uncatchable neutral particle to carry off the energy and angular momentum missing from beta decay; after Chadwick found the neutron in 1932 Fermi named this one the neutrino, and Fermi's 1933 theory of beta decay built on it, which is where the weak interaction starts. From 1935 he held the theoretical physics chair at the ETH in Zurich, spent the war years lecturing in America and went back in 1946. In 1940 he proved spin and statistics must be welded together — whole spins cluster, half-spins refuse one another — and the 1945 Nobel Prize named a single achievement, the exclusion principle. He argued with Einstein for thirty years about whether quantum mechanics was complete, and he was among the very few who could corner Bohr and Heisenberg in public. Jung analysed something like a thousand of his dreams while they probed whether matter and mind might share one underlying order. His cruelty became a term of art — of one manuscript he pronounced the verdict not even wrong; when a spectrograph blew up in Göttingen in 1931 colleagues blamed his presence, and gear that fails around him is still said to show the Pauli effect. Pancreatic cancer killed him in Zurich on 15 December 1958, aged 58.

oneLiner: 从费米统计到第一座反应堆，理论与手艺俱佳的那个人。
oneLinerEn: From Fermi statistics to the first reactor: theory and craft in one person.
detail: 他 14 岁丧兄，靠少年时与兄长合抄的一位修士的拉丁文数理手稿自学，1922 年在比萨毕业，1926 年 24 岁当上罗马大学理论物理教授，带着一屋子年轻人（拉塞蒂、塞格雷、阿马尔迪、马约拉纳）上山徒步讨论物理，人称帕尼佩尔纳街学派。同年他给自旋为半整数的粒子写出新统计，与狄拉克各自独立完成：金属里的电子、白矮星里的物质都按费米-狄拉克分布排队，一类粒子因此叫费米子。1933 年他把 β 衰变写成四个费米子在同一顶点耦合的理论（稿子先被《自然》退回，理由是离现实太远），并给那个失踪能量的粒子定了中微子之名——弱相互作用第一个能用的形式就是它。1934 年起他用中子挨个轰击元素，意外发现含氢物质慢化中子会让诱导放射性放大几十倍，做出四十多种人工放射性核，并宣布找到了 92 号之后的超铀元素；1938 年 12 月他因中子辐照产生新放射性元素获诺贝尔奖，同一年哈恩与施特拉斯曼证明的其实是铀核裂变，那个发现离他的实验台只有一步。领奖后他携犹太裔妻子劳拉直接去了纽约，没有再回墨索里尼的意大利。1942 年 12 月 2 日下午，芝加哥大学橄榄球场看台下的 CP-1 达到自持链式反应，运行二十八分钟，现场向华盛顿发电报说意大利导航员已安全登陆。在洛斯阿拉莫斯他是少数既算得动又能上手的人：三位一体核试时他撒落纸片、凭飘送的距离估出当量，量级正确；他是唯一同时在场于首次链式反应、首次原子弹爆炸与首次氢弹原理试验的人。1949 年他主持的顾问委员会曾建议拒绝氢弹，1951 年新的分级构型说服了他，此后他投入热核工作。战后他在芝加哥做加速器与宇宙线，1950 年一次午餐闲聊里追问「可他们到底在哪儿呢」，二十多年后被写成费米悖论；他教的「先估数量级再动笔」（比萨有多少个厨师？）今天还在面试卷上，叫费米估算。1954 年 11 月 28 日他因胃癌在芝加哥去世，第 100 号元素以他命名。
detailEn: He lost his brother at fourteen, taught himself from Latin math notes he and the boy had copied out of a friar's manuscript, took his Pisa degree in 1922, and in 1926 became professor of theoretical physics in Rome at twenty-four, gathering Rasetti, Segrè, Amaldi and Majorana into a group that argued physics on mountain walks — the boys of via Panisperna. That same year he wrote the statistics for half-integer-spin particles, independently of Dirac: the electrons in a metal and the matter in a white dwarf queue up by the Fermi-Dirac distribution, and a whole family of particles is named fermions after him. In 1933 he cast beta decay as four fermions coupled at one vertex — Nature rejected the letter as too remote from reality — and gave the particle that carried the missing energy its name, the neutrino; the first usable form of the weak interaction is that theory. From 1934 he bombarded element after element with neutrons, found by accident that hydrogen-rich material slowed them and multiplied induced radioactivity tens of times, made some forty artificial radioisotopes, and announced elements beyond uranium; in December 1938 he was awarded the Nobel Prize for new radioactive elements from neutron irradiation, in the same year Hahn and Strassmann were proving that the uranium nucleus had split, a discovery within a step of his own bench. He and his Jewish wife Laura sailed from Stockholm to New York and he never returned to Mussolini's Italy. On the afternoon of 2 December 1942 the pile called CP-1 under the stands of Chicago's Stagg Field went self-sustaining for twenty-eight minutes, and the site cabled Washington that the Italian navigator had landed safely. At Los Alamos he was one of the few who could both calculate and build: at the Trinity test he dropped confetti and read the blast yield off how far the wind took it, getting the order of magnitude right, and he is the only person present at the first chain reaction, the first atomic explosion and the first thermonuclear device. In 1949 the committee he chaired advised against the hydrogen bomb; the staged configuration of 1951 changed his mind and he worked on it. After the war at Chicago he ran accelerator and cosmic-ray physics, and at a 1950 lunch he asked between courses where all the visitors were — a question later written up as the Fermi paradox. His habit of estimating the order of magnitude before writing anything down (how many cooks are there in Pisa?) survives on interview sheets as the Fermi estimate. Stomach cancer killed him in Chicago on 28 November 1954; element 100 is named fermium.

oneLiner: 一周之内把电流的磁效应变成一门电动力学，电流单位归他。
oneLinerEn: One week turned the magnetic effect of currents into electrodynamics; the ampere is his.
detail: 他 1775 年生在里昂的富商之家，1793 年父亲被革命法庭送上断头台，他靠家里的三千册藏书自学，十二岁读完多卷《百科全书》，后来又自己补拉丁文去读欧拉与伯努利的原著，据说能整本倒背。1801 年他在布尔教书，写论文想把道尔顿的原子论与盖-吕萨克的气体化合体积比调和起来，思路通到阿伏加德罗后来分清的那个原子-分子之别，只是没人读。1804 年他到巴黎，1820 年 9 月奥斯特发现通电导线能让磁针偏转的消息经《科学年鉴》传到法国，10 月 9 日阿拉戈在科学院当场演示；安培一周之内就把问题换了：不是电生磁，而是电流与电流也互相作用——同向相吸、反向相斥，并给出可叠加定量的经验定律。他把这门新学问命名为电动力学，把磁全部解释成物质内部环流的分子电流，从此不必再假想两种磁荷；他造出电流天平去量两股电流之间的力，把新绕的线圈叫作螺线管，这门学问的词多半出自他手；他又把电流方向定为从正极流向负极，沿用至今。1822 到 1826 年的《电动力学现象的数学理论》把他的定律写成沿闭合回路的积分形式，麦克斯韦把它收进方程组并添上位移电流，今天课本上叫安培环路定律。他做的线圈与磁针实验让电话与电动机的原理有了一句话的根据；欧姆 1827 年的工作用的正是安培定下的电流测量约定。1824 年起他在法兰西公学院任实验物理教授，1831 年兼任大学理科总督学，1836 年 6 月 10 日在去热那亚的路上病死于马赛一家旅馆，儿子阿尔弗雷德陪到最后。1948 年国际计量大会把电流单位定作安培，写成相距一米的两条无限长平行导线之间每米 2×10⁻⁷ 牛的力；2019 年单位重新定义后，它改为由基本电荷的固定数值给出——全世界的电表上仍有他的名字。
detailEn: Born in Lyon in 1775 to a prosperous merchant family, he watched the Revolution send his father to the guillotine in 1793 and taught himself out of the three thousand volumes at home: the whole Encyclopédie by twelve, Latin picked up later so as to read Euler and Bernoulli in the original, with a memory for reciting books backwards. He was a school teacher in Bourg in 1801 and wrote a paper trying to reconcile Dalton's atoms with Gay-Lussac's combining volumes of gases, one step short of the atom-molecule distinction Avogadro later made, and nobody read it. He came to Paris in 1804. When Oersted's news that a currented wire deflects a needle reached France through the Annales de Chimie, Arago showed it to the Institute on 9 October 1820; inside weeks Ampère had changed the question — not whether electricity makes magnetism, but that currents act on currents too, attracting when parallel and repelling when antiparallel, with an empirical force law that could be added up circuit by circuit. He named the new subject electrodynamics, explained all magnetism as molecular currents circulating inside matter so that two kinds of magnetic fluid were no longer needed, and he built a current balance to weigh the push between two currents and named the new coil a solenoid — much of the subject's vocabulary is his — while fixing current's direction as flowing from positive to negative, which is still how the arrow is drawn. His Théorie mathématique of 1822 to 1826 put his law into the integral round a closed circuit that Maxwell kept in the equations after adding the displacement current, and which textbooks now call Ampère's circuital law: the coil and the needle, in one sentence, are the ancestor of every motor and relay. Ohm's 1827 work rests on the current scale Ampère had fixed. He took the chair of experimental physics at the Collège de France in 1824 and became inspector general of university science in 1831; he died of fever in a Marseille inn on 10 June 1836, on the road to Genoa, with his son Alfred at the bedside. In 1948 the CGPM made the ampere the base unit of current, defined as the current that, sent through two long parallel wires a metre apart in vacuum, gives each metre of the other a push of 2×10⁻⁷ newtons; since the 2019 restatement it comes from a fixed value of the elementary charge — his name is on every ammeter on earth.

oneLiner: 把熵写成微观状态数的对数，为原子论赌上一生的人。
oneLinerEn: Entropy as the logarithm of microstates: the man who staked his life on atoms.
detail: 他 1844 年生在维也纳，1867 年在维也纳大学拿博士学位，25 岁经斯特藩推荐去做格拉茨的数学物理教授，此后一生在格拉茨、维也纳、慕尼黑、莱比锡之间来回，最后坐回维也纳的理论物理教席。1866 年他把麦克斯韦的速度分布推广到有外力场的情形，写出课本上的那个指数因子 e 的 −E/kT 次方；1872 年给出输运方程与 H 定理：分子碰撞让分布单调走向平衡，「时间为什么只朝一个方向走」第一次有了力学说法，而他清楚这套推理的前提是分子真的存在。1877 年他把熵写成 S = k log W，无序度等于微观状态数取对数，热力学第二定律从铁律降级为「几乎必然」的统计命题；1884 年他用热力学加上麦克斯韦的辐射压强推出斯特藩的 T⁴ 定律。1890 年代他与马赫、奥斯特瓦尔德的唯能论正面开战：对方说原子只是记账的方便符号，他在 1897 年发表《自然科学中原子论的必要性》，反驳原子论已经能解释扩散、渗透压与气体比热；那几年欧洲多数物理学家站在对手一边。1900 年普朗克在黑体公式里借用他这条对数关系，才不得不引入能量子，普朗克自述这一步走得极不情愿、挣扎了好几年，给常数 k 定名并算出数值的也正是普朗克。1890 年代他在达尔马提亚度假时曾试图自杀未遂，此后情绪时起时伏，1900 年仍应邀去耶鲁做系列讲演。1906 年 9 月 5 日，在的里雅斯特附近的多伊诺，他用浴巾结束了自己的生命，62 岁。爱因斯坦 1905 年从分子碰撞推出布朗运动、佩兰 1908 年把它量成原子的证据，都已在他身后。他的维也纳中央公墓墓碑上只刻一行：S = k log W。埃伦费斯特在维也纳做过他的助教，接过了这门统计物理的讲义。
detailEn: Born in Vienna in 1844, doctorate there in 1867, at twenty-five he was recommended by Josef Stefan to the chair of mathematical physics at Graz, and spent the rest of his life shuttling between Graz, Vienna, Munich and Leipzig before returning to Vienna's theoretical physics chair. In 1866 he extended Maxwell's velocity distribution to fields of force and wrote down the exponential factor e to the power −E/kT found in every textbook; in 1872 came his transport equation and the H-theorem, which make the collision of molecules drive a distribution monotonically toward equilibrium and give, for the first time, a mechanical account of why time has one direction only — with the premise, which he never disguised, that the molecules are real. In 1877 he wrote entropy as S = k log W, disorder being the logarithm of the count of microstates, demoting the second law from iron rule to a proposition that is only almost certain. In 1884, from thermodynamics plus Maxwell's radiation pressure, he derived Stefan's fourth-power law. Through the 1890s he fought Mach and Ostwald's energetism head-on: they called atoms a bookkeeping convenience, and his 1897 answer On the Necessity of the Atomic Theory in Natural Science listed diffusion, osmotic pressure and gas specific heats as work only atoms could do, while most physicists of Europe sided with his opponents. In 1900 Planck borrowed this very logarithmic relation to interpolate his black-body formula and found himself forced to quantise energy — an act he described as unhappily desperate, argued over for years — and it was Planck in the same work who named and measured the constant k. Boltzmann had attempted suicide while on holiday in Dalmatia in the 1890s, and his moods rose and fell after that; he still gave the Yale lecture series in 1900. On 5 September 1906, at Duino near Trieste, he killed himself with a bath towel, aged 62. Einstein's 1905 account of Brownian motion as molecular bombardment and Perrin's measurements, published in 1908, came after him. His gravestone in the Vienna Zentralfriedhof carries one line: S = k log W. Ehrenfest, his assistant in Vienna, carried the statistical physics forward.
